title: Carrington Event (great geomagnetic storm of 1859)
summary: A great geomagnetic storm ran from 28 August to 3 September 1859. On 1 September Richard Carrington saw a white-light solar flare, and about seventeen hours later auroras reached as far south as Panama. About 200,000 km of telegraph line worldwide was affected, many lines unusable for 8 hours or more.

uncertainty.note: Storm interval 28 August to 3 September 1859; the white-light flare was recorded on 1 September. Pin year set to 1859.

as_recorded.value: on September 1, English astronomer Richard C. Carrington

importance.justification: The benchmark extreme space-weather event and the first link observed between solar flares and aurora.
